name: Ample Classes Are Closed under Projecting Common-Section Gluing
statement: Let ample pieces $A_i\subseteq Q_{E\sqcup F_i}$ have pairwise disjoint private coordinate blocks, contain the same zero section $D$, and project onto exactly $D$ in the shared coordinates. Their embedded union $A_1\oplus_D\cdots\oplus_D A_m$ is ample. Moreover, projection to the common coordinates is the Hamming gate onto $D$ in each piece; when every shared coordinate varies on $D$, the gate property conversely forces the projection condition.
proof: A support shattered by the union cannot meet two private blocks, since the trace assigning one in each such block is absent. It therefore lies in one shared-plus-private coordinate block, where the union projects to the corresponding ample piece; that piece supplies a positioned cube. The gate identity separates shared and private Hamming contributions. Conversely, disagreement between a proposed gate and the projected word in a varying shared coordinate makes the coordinatewise triangle inequality strict for a suitable point of $D$.
